# Generated by `cafe gen chart` from this project's cafaye.yml.

# parlor

The Helm chart parlor is deployed from. The templates are the
contract; `values.yaml` is the deployment-time half — the file the
values commit edits.

## The loop

The chart is deployed by ArgoCD, pull-only, and the Application is
not this chart's: the substrate owns it — one static Application
per service, OCI-sourced, applied by install.sh (cafaye/notes/deployment.md,
"Who owns the Application"). A service repository commits none.
The only thing that can change the cluster is a commit: push a
values commit, Argo syncs, the box agrees with git. A hand edit
self-heals; rollback is `git revert`.

## Shipping the chart

The chart ships from the fleet's private OCI registry, because the
substrate is closed source and a pull-based system needs somewhere to
pull from:

    helm package chart
    helm push chart-0.1.0.tgz oci://ghcr.io/cafaye/charts/parlor

The box pulls it with the read-only secret `values.yaml` names
(`imagePullSecrets`), created on the box once, out of band. The chart
names the secret and never contains a credential.

## Secrets

The service's environment arrives by reference: the Deployment reads
the secret `values.yaml` names (`secretName`) with `envFrom`. Create
it on the box:

    kubectl create secret generic parlor-secrets --from-literal=...

Rotate a value by replacing the secret and restarting the pods — not
by editing a generated file.

## Reaching the service

The chart installs no Ingress until a values commit says so, and
**parlor's values commit says so**: `ingress.enabled` is `true` in
`values.yaml`, with `helm template` rendering the Ingress below. With
`enabled` false the same template emits no Ingress at all — a chart
that suddenly routes traffic is a defect — and with `enabled` true
and empty `hosts` (and empty legacy `host`) the template `fail`s,
because an Ingress with no host is a silent misroute. Both red
controls are asserted in `src/lib/chart.test.ts`.

parlor's hosts are **`app.cafaye.com`** (the product), **`cafaye.com`**
(apex) and **`www.cafaye.com`** — the host the fleet's own fixtures
name (`billing/test/fixtures/stripe/checkout.session.completed*.json`
carries `https://app.cafaye.com/welcome`) plus the apex and www that
serve the marketing landing and the `/box/install` front door. That
front door is `curl -fsSL https://cafaye.com/box/install | bash` —
every doc, the `/box` page and `cafe box init` print it — and it must
never 301 away again (see `chart/values.yaml` and fix/apex-hosts).

    ingress:
      enabled: true
      hosts:
        - app.cafaye.com
        - cafaye.com
        - www.cafaye.com
      clusterIssuer: letsencrypt-prod
      tls: true

`className` is traefik, k3s's default (DEPLOYMENT.md:28). The
ClusterIssuer is created once per cluster by the substrate (kit's
install, step 7), not by the chart — the chart only NAMES it, the
same "names the secret and never contains a credential" discipline
the imagePullSecrets block uses. `tls: true` writes the `spec.tls`
block with one entry per host and cert-manager provisions each
certificate into `parlor-tls-<host>` (dots → dashes, e.g.
`parlor-tls-app-cafaye-com`). Without an issuer there is no TLS: a
secret nothing writes. `host` (singular) remains as a deprecated
alias for back-compat; `hosts` takes precedence.

## Readiness

The probe is `/readyz`. That is the fleet's contract: every cafaye
service serves it, and the rollout waits on it. It is baked into the
template rather than left as a value, because a readiness path that
can be edited is a readiness path that can be pointed at `/up` — the
defect the kamal template had, which produced deploys that could
never go green.
